<svg viewBox="0 0 320 210" role="img" aria-label="The quadratic formula labelled part by part: x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, all divided by two a. The plus or minus produces the two roots, the expression under the root is the discriminant that counts them, and the two a divides the entire numerator." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="50" y="108" fill="var(--text)" font-size="14" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="end">x =</text>
<text x="90" y="94" fill="var(--accent)" font-size="14" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="start">-b ±</text>
<text x="132" y="94" fill="var(--code-accent)" font-size="14" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="start">√(b² - 4ac)</text>
<line x1="82" y1="102" x2="234" y2="102" stroke="var(--text)" stroke-width="2" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="158" y="124" fill="var(--accent-2)" font-size="14" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">2a</text>
<line x1="176" y1="78" x2="176" y2="60" stroke="var(--code-accent)" stroke-width="1.4" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="176" y="52" fill="var(--code-accent)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">the discriminant counts the roots</text>
<line x1="116" y1="98" x2="80" y2="136" stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="1.4" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="76" y="150" fill="var(--accent)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">± gives both roots</text>
<line x1="170" y1="128" x2="238" y2="150" stroke="var(--accent-2)" stroke-width="1.4" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="300" y="164" fill="var(--accent-2)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="600" text-anchor="end">2a divides all of it</text>
<text x="160" y="192" fill="var(--text-2)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" text-anchor="middle">D > 0: two roots    D = 0: one root    D < 0: none</text>
</svg>
caption: Every part of the formula does one job, and the fraction bar reaches across the whole numerator.

name: mcr3u-rational-exponents_0
svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 210" role="img" aria-label="The anatomy of x to the power m over n: the numerator m is the power and the denominator n is the root index, so 8 to the two thirds means take the cube root of 8 to get 2, then square it to get 4" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<defs><marker id="rex-a" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="var(--code-accent)"/></marker><marker id="rex-b" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="var(--accent-2)"/></marker></defs>
<text x="160" y="22" fill="var(--text-2)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" text-anchor="middle">how to read a fractional exponent</text>
<text x="100" y="102" fill="var(--text)" font-size="40" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">x</text>
<text x="136" y="76" fill="var(--code-accent)" font-size="18" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">m</text>
<line x1="124" y1="82" x2="148" y2="82" stroke="var(--text-2)" stroke-width="1.6" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="136" y="102" fill="var(--accent-2)" font-size="18" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">n</text>
<line x1="152" y1="70" x2="192" y2="54" stroke="var(--code-accent)" stroke-width="1.6" marker-end="url(#rex-a)" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="198" y="52" fill="var(--code-accent)" font-size="11" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="600" text-anchor="start">the power</text>
<line x1="152" y1="100" x2="192" y2="118" stroke="var(--accent-2)" stroke-width="1.6" marker-end="url(#rex-b)" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="198" y="122" fill="var(--accent-2)" font-size="11" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="600" text-anchor="start">which root</text>
<line x1="30" y1="146" x2="290" y2="146" stroke="var(--border)" stroke-width="1" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
<text x="160" y="172" fill="var(--accent)" font-size="13" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">8^(2/3)  ->  cube root 8 = 2  ->  2^2 = 4</text>
<text x="160" y="192" fill="var(--text-2)" font-size="10" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace" text-anchor="middle">root first, power second: the numbers stay small</text>
</svg>
caption: The bottom of the exponent chooses the root and the top chooses the power, so the cube root comes before the squaring.

name: mcr3u-inverse-function_0
caption: The inverse is the original curve reflected in the line y = x, so every point (a, b) becomes (b, a).

name: mcr3u-transform-quadratic_0
caption: The parent y = x² is flipped and doubled, so its 1, 3, 5 step pattern becomes down 2, down 6, down 10 from the vertex.

name: mcr3u-transform-radical_0
caption: A negative k turns the curve to face left, so the domain runs x ≤ 3 instead of x ≥ 3.

name: mcr3u-transform-reciprocal_0
caption: The asymptotes cross at (d, c) = (-3, -3), and each branch hugs them without ever touching.

name: mdm4u-confidence-intervals_0

name: mdm4u-distribution-shapes_0
caption: Skew is named for the tail, not the hump, and the mean is always the measure dragged furthest towards it.

name: mdm4u-normal-basics_0
caption: The empirical rule: 68 percent within one standard deviation, 95 percent within two, 99.7 percent within three, leaving 2.5 percent in each tail beyond two.

name: mdm4u-spread_0
caption: Identical means, very different spreads: the average tells you nothing about how far a typical value strays from it.

name: mdm4u-z-scores_0
caption: A z-table hands you the shaded area to the left of z; the right tail is whatever is left over after subtracting from 1.
